title: 第19章 棋局第20章 杜家变故
content_zh:
二更天已过，杜府上下笼罩在浓稠的夜色中。
杜若和宝儿正从杜五娘院子回到自己院里。
一个丫鬟提着灯笼匆匆赶来，朝杜若福了一福：“七娘子，老爷请您去棋室。”
“宝儿，你回我屋里将熏香点上，我同爹下完棋回来好睡觉。”
杜若与宝儿互视了一眼，宝儿应声“是”，杜若整了整衣襟，跟着那丫鬟往前院走去。
等杜若跟着那丫鬟走远了，宝儿身形一转，化作君澜模样，无声无息地隐入了廊下的阴影中。
棋室在正堂东侧，是一间不大的暖阁，平日里杜茂源极少让人进去，今夜却灯火通明，门户大敞，像是特意在等什么人。杜若跨进门的时候，杜茂源已经在里面了。他换了一身粗布的青色蓝袍，腰间束着一条素带，少了平日的威严，倒显出几分居家之态。棋盘已经摆好，黑白两子分置两侧，他坐在西首端着茶盏，听见脚步声抬眼看过来：“来了，坐。”
杜若在他对面坐下，目光扫过棋盘，棋盘上还没有落子，黑白分明，像两军对垒前的寂静。
“爹，这么晚了还没歇息？”
“睡不着。”杜茂源将茶盏搁下，拎起一枚白子在指尖转了转，“你平安从闽地回家，又碰上柳氏的丧礼，爹还没好好跟你说过话，今日有空下一局。”
杜若没有推辞，起一枚黑子落在右上角。杜茂源随即落子，手法娴熟，不紧不慢。
他的棋风和他这个人一样沉稳老辣，每一步都像是在下一盘很大的棋，不急于一时的得失，却在不经意间将对手逼入绝境。
“这一次，你考虑很久了。”杜茂源看着杜若悬在半空的手。
杜若将黑子落在左下角，声音平静。这一手不占边角不取实地，看似落了下风，实则暗藏杀机。
杜茂源看了一眼，嘴角微微一动：“几日不见，你棋艺大有长进。”
“虎父无犬女。”杜若讨好地笑。
杜茂源被恭维得很是受用，将白子落下：“爹就喜欢你这张嘴，说话得人心。”
棋室内安静下来，只有棋子落在棋盘上的清脆声响，间或夹杂着茶盏与桌面触碰的轻响。
窗外夜风阵阵，吹着院中的桂花树沙沙作响，几片枯叶从半开的窗扉间飘进来，落在棋盘边。
杜茂源伸手去拂落叶，随意得像在说家常话：“五娘的事，你不用担心。”

“五娘去闽地，除了祈福，还有旁的事吗？”
棋子落在棋盘上，“啪”的一声。
杜茂源抬起头看着杜若，目光在他脸上停留了片刻，然后笑了，那笑容很淡，不是敷衍，倒像是一种试探之后的确认：
“你五姐的事，就不必操心了。她是个有主意的孩子，比你想的要聪明得多。她既然主动请缨，为父自然要成全。”
“可是爹，那海上……女儿能回来真是九死一生。”
“为父也乏了。”杜茂源搁下茶站起身来，“这一局先记着，明日再续。”
杜若只好起身福了一福，目送杜茂源走出棋室。
她回到棋盘前，低头看着那盘未完的棋局。
窗外风又大了些，吹得灯笼晃晃悠悠，夜风裹着深秋的凉意灌进来，杜若打了个寒噤。
她看着门外的夜色，不知道君澜找到杜五娘了没有。
content_en:
The second watch has passed, and the whole Du Mansion is shrouded in thick night.
Du Ruo and Bao'er were returning to their own courtyard from Du Wuniang's courtyard.
A maid hurried over with a lantern and greeted Du Ruofu: "Seventh lady, I invite you to go to the chess room."
"Bao'er, you go back to my room and light the incense. I'll come back from playing chess with dad so I can sleep."
Du Ruo and Bao'er looked at each other, and Bao'er responded "Yes". Du Ruo straightened his clothes and followed the maid to the front yard.
When Du Ruo followed the maid and walked away, Bao'er turned around, transformed into Jun Lan, and disappeared silently into the shadows of the corridor.
The chess room is on the east side of the main hall. It is a small warm pavilion. On weekdays, Du Maoyuan rarely lets people in, but tonight it is brightly lit and the door is wide open, as if he is specially waiting for someone. When Du Ruo stepped through the door, Du Maoyuan was already inside. He changed into a green and blue robe of coarse cloth, with a plain belt tied around his waist. He lacked his usual majesty and looked more like a homely person. The chessboard had been set up, and the black and white pieces were placed on both sides. He was sitting at the west end holding a tea cup. When he heard the footsteps, he looked up and said, "Here you go, sit down."
Du Ruo sat down opposite him and glanced at the chessboard. There was no move on the chessboard yet, and it was clear black and white, like the silence before a confrontation between two armies.
"Dad, it's so late and you haven't rested yet?"
"Can't sleep." Du Maoyuan put down the tea cup, picked up a white coin and turned it around at his fingertips, "You came home safely from Fujian, and it happened to be Liu's funeral. Dad hasn't spoken to you properly yet, so I have time to play another game today."
Du Ruo didn't refuse, and a sunspot landed on the upper right corner. Du Maoyuan immediately made his move, skillfully and unhurriedly.
His chess style is as calm and sophisticated as the person he is. Every move is like playing a big game of chess. He is not anxious for temporary gains and losses, but inadvertently forces his opponent into a desperate situation.
"This time, you have been thinking about it for a long time." Du Maoyuan looked at Du Ruo's hand hanging in the air.
Du Ruo placed the sunspot in the lower left corner with a calm voice. This move does not take advantage of the corners and does not take the real ground. It seems to be at a disadvantage, but in fact it hides murderous intent.
Du Maoyuan glanced at him and twitched the corner of his mouth slightly: "I haven't seen you for a few days. Your chess skills have improved a lot."
"Tiger father has no dog daughter." Du Ruo smiled flatteringly.
Du Maoyuan was very pleased with the compliment and put down the white piece: "Dad likes your mouth, you speak to win people's hearts."
The chess room became quiet, with only the crisp sound of chess pieces falling on the chessboard, occasionally mixed with the soft sound of tea cups touching the table.
The night wind outside the window rustled the sweet-scented osmanthus tree in the courtyard, and a few dead leaves drifted in from the half-opened window and landed next to the chessboard.
Du Maoyuan stretched out his hand to brush the fallen leaves, and said casually as if he was talking at home: "You don't have to worry about Wu Niang's affairs."
"When Wu Niang goes to Fujian, besides praying for blessings, is there anything else to do?"
The chess piece landed on the chessboard with a "pop" sound.
Du Maoyuan raised his head and looked at Du Ruo, his eyes stayed on his face for a moment, and then he smiled. The smile was very light, not perfunctory, but like a confirmation after testing:
"You don't have to worry about your fifth sister. She is a child with ideas, much smarter than you think. Since she took the initiative to ask for help, her father will naturally fulfill her wish."
"But dad, on the sea... it's a narrow escape for my daughter to come back."
"I am tired of being a father." Du Maoyuan put down his tea and stood up, "Remember this game for now and continue tomorrow."
Du Ruo had no choice but to get up and say a blessing and watched Du Maoyuan walk out of the chess room.
She returned to the chessboard and looked down at the unfinished game.
The wind outside the window became stronger again, causing the lanterns to sway. The night breeze came in with the coolness of late autumn, and Du Ruo shivered.
She looked at the night outside the door, wondering if Jun Lan had found Du Wuniang.
